rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 (find root cause → write tests → run+confirm fail → fix → run again → show diff) and prompt 3 (write failing test → run+watch fail → fix → run again+watch pass → show diff) each carry 5 named sub-steps, meeting the rule's own structural trigger ("4+ named sub-steps"). Read both registry files directly: neither carries an in-fence "No preamble." suppressor as its last line, and no body primer after either fence names the preamble-then-skim-past cue. Harm is real but modest: on a 25-minute trivial-bug exercise, a few sentences of Claude narration before the first tool call is pacing friction, not a comprehension break or a misleading result.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a trailing in-fence line — e.g. "No preamble. Start by writing the test." — to prompt-1 and prompt-3, or add a short body primer after each fence naming the narrate-then-act pattern and telling the student to skim past the opening sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reference-doc / plan.md / SKILL.md / verifier-script authoring task in this file; the artifacts are ordinary code + tests + a PR, not a standalone knowledge-artifact needing a pre-save grill.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts 1 and 3 both end "Show me the diff before you commit." — literally the pre-confirm shape this rule generally discourages in favour of post-action report. This is a deliberate, correct exception rather than a violation: the review-and-pushback beat (section 2, "Read the diff and push back on a line" — "**The point:** pushing back is core work") is this exercise's entire forcing function and must happen BEFORE the commit lands, not after (a post-commit "tell me what you committed" would force an amend/revert cycle to implement pushback, breaking the exercise's own design). The rule's named carve-out list (production deploys, mass email, payment moves) doesn't literally name this case, but the underlying reason — the review gate IS the taught skill, not a confirmation reflex — matches the same family as this compendium's own §20 (grill-before-save) and §35 (gate writes until an explicit trigger). Filing a REVISE and "fixing" it to post-action would degrade the artefact, so per the dispatch preamble this is reported as PASS with the boundary named rather than flagged.
